text.en: This Act may be cited as the Legislative Council and Council of Ministers (Remuneration and Privileges) Act.

(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires"Member" means a person appointed, nominated or elected, as the case may be, to the Legislative Council pursuant to or under the Constitution or a Member of the Council of Ministers, and includes the Speaker; • "specified duty" means a meeting of the Legislative Council or any Committee thereof or a meeting of the Council of Ministers or any committee thereof and includes such other meetings or duties as may be specified by His Majesty the Sultan and Yang

(2) Where there is any doubt as to the interpretation or construction • of this Act, the question shall be referred to His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan whose decision thereon shall be final. LAWS OF BRUNEI • 4 CAP. 134 and Privileges) [S 46105}
His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan may by order make provision for the remuneration of Members of the Legislative Council and of • the Council ofMinisters. etc. of remuneration.

The remuneration payable under the provisions of section 3 shall -

(a) commence from the date of appointment or election, whichever is the case;

(b) accrue from day to day; and

(c) be payable on the last day of each month or such other day as the Minister may determine. on Consolidated Fund.
The moneys required for the remunerations payable under this Act shall be a charge on the Consolidated Fund. of Schedule.

His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan may by order published add to or amend the Schedule to this Act. • • • 3) • ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES OF MEMBERS of the Legislative Council are authorised to transmit free of charge all correspondence on Government business. The correspondence should be enclosed in envelopes marked "ON GOVERNMENT SERVICE" and the bottom left hand comer of the envelopes shall be signed by the Member sending the letter over a "chop" "MEMBER OF THE LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL". The privilege will cover correspondence within Brunei Darussalam only and it will not include the right to frank registered articles or airmail When an article, airmail, correspondence or any telegram is required to be sent or a trunk be made by a Member on Government business, the cost incurred thereby may be recovered.

Travelling outside Brunei Darussalam: A Member required to travel outside Brunei Darussalam on Government business by sea or air may with the approval of the Minister or an officer authorised by him in that regard, be granted a travel warrant and the cost of such travel shall be paid by the Government.

Motor vehicle badges: A Member using his own motor vehicle or a motor vehicle placed at his disposal for his use may carry on such vehicle a distinctive badge or badges in such form as may be authorised by His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan.

Medical facilities: A Member, his wife, children and parents (including parent-in-law) shall be entitled to free medical and dental treatments including specialist treatment and to admission to first-class ward, or, in default of any such eligibility, to reimbursement of any sum expended by him or such treatment.

Telephone:

(1) Members are each entitled to have a telephone installed free of charge at their of residence. The Director of Telecommunications will make arrangements to install the telephone provided such installation is practicable. •

(2) A Member who uses a telephone at his normal place of residence may recover from the Government the charges for telephone rentals (but excluding trunk call charges) for the telephone during his tenure of office as a Member: Provided that a Member who is enjoying the use of a telephone free of charge by virtue of any other Government appointment may not be granted this privilege.

Subsistence allowance: [S 46/05} • The Speaker, Ministers and Deputy Ministers will be entitled to subsistence allowances at the same rates and subject to the same conditions as an officer in Division I of the public A Member, other than the Speaker, a Minister or a Deputy Minister, may be paid a subsistence allowance at the rate notified in the Gazette. •

Resthouse and Holiday Bungalows: A Member shall be entitled to the same privileges in respect of Government Resthouse and Holiday Bungalows as accorded to an officer in Division I of the public service. •
Priorities: A Member shall be entitled to the same priorities in respect of all public utilities and services as are accorded to an officer in Division I of the public service.
Honorific: A Member shall be entitled to the appellation of "The Honourable" preceding his name . • •
